---
title: "The PyLabRobot Cookbook"
---

A task-indexed manual for [PyLabRobot](https://github.com/PyLabRobot/pylabrobot) **0.2.2**.

If you know Python and have never used PLR, Parts I and II get you writing working protocols.
Parts III and IV are for people building something that has to keep running.

## How to read this

- **[Recipe index](recipes.qmd)** — every recipe in the book, indexed by task and searchable by
  the API it uses. This is the page to bookmark.
- **[Cheat sheet](CHEATSHEET.qmd)** — flat lookup: function, signature, one line.
- **Parts I–II** — broad coverage of PLR's everyday surface. Read straight through once.
- **Part III** — the cross-cutting concerns: error recovery, logging, testing, data, config.
- **Part IV** — two guided builds, start to finish, every step given.

## Everything here runs without a robot

Every snippet executes against `LiquidHandlerChatterboxBackend`, which simulates a liquid handler
by narrating what it would do. Nothing in Parts I–III needs hardware.

```{python}
#| eval: false
import pylabrobot
print(pylabrobot.__version__)   # 0.2.2
```

::: {.callout-important}
## This book targets 0.2.2 specifically

PLR changes across minor versions, sometimes by deleting things. Liquid identity tracking and the
cross-contamination tracker were removed before 0.2.2; the `main` branch has since moved the entire
liquid handling stack under `pylabrobot.legacy` as part of the v1b1 migration.

Recipes are written and executed against **0.2.2**. Pin it:

```bash
pip install "pylabrobot==0.2.2"
```
:::

## Conventions

| You will see | It means |
|---|---|
| A **Gotcha** warning callout | a way this bites people in practice |
| An **important** callout | a conceptual point that changes how you read the rest |
| A **Python you need here** margin note | the language feature the recipe leans on — skippable on a first read |
| Numbered code annotations | hover or click the ① markers beside a line |

::: {.callout-warning}
## Gotcha

Warning callouts look like this. Every one is a real failure mode, not a style note.
:::
